Extract the nugget of an estimated autocorrelation range

Source: R/cross-validation.R
sac_nugget.Rd

The nugget variance of the variogram model behind an estimate_sac_range() result: the model's semivariance as the separation shrinks to zero, which is measurement error plus variation at scales shorter than the first lag of the empirical variogram.

Usage

sac_nugget(x)

Arguments

x

A sac_range object, or any other value.

Value

A single number, the nugget in the units of the response's variance, or NA_real_ when x carries no fitted model: a bare NA from a run that could not fit anything, a rejected result with too few lag bins to fit, or an object that is not a sac_range.

Details

The nugget is extrapolated to zero from the first lag, not observed, so it is only as good as that lag is short; attr(x, "first_lag") says where the extrapolation starts. With lags = "adaptive" (the default) the first lag is the separation of the closest pairs of points. With lags = "equal" it is the middle of a bin cutoff * max_dist / n_lags wide, which on a dense layer can be many times the spacing of close pairs, and structure shorter than that bin is then counted as nugget. When attr(x, "lag_fallback") is TRUE the result is the equal-lag one although adaptive lags were asked for (see the section "The lags" in estimate_sac_range()), and its nugget is extrapolated from the first equal bin.

Every classed result, identified or rejected, carries the nugget as its nugget attribute, since a resolution criterion for a tessellation needs it: it is the short-lag variance that no cell can average away. On a result refused for want of spatial structure it is the variance of the modelled variable, the nugget of the pure-nugget model that the refusal supports.

How far to trust it

Four more attributes of the result bear on the nugget.

  • nugget_at_bound is TRUE when the fit put the nugget at its lower bound (0, or at most 1e-4 of the sill). That value is the bound and not an estimate, and a criterion that uses it as a noise variance has no penalty left. A nugget equal to its floor (see nugget_floor) is the variance between visits, a measurement, and nugget_at_bound stays FALSE for it unless the floor itself is at most 1e-4 of the sill.

  • short_lag_semivariance is the semivariance of nearest-neighbour pairs of locations, computed with no model; short_lag_pairs and short_lag_dist give the number of pairs and their median separation. Each location is paired with the nearest other location, and of several whose squared distances agree to one part in ten million, with the one of lower x coordinate, then lower y. On a square lattice that pairs almost every location with its neighbour along x, so the value measures the field along x, and with the axes of the CRS swapped it can differ. A semivariance does not fall as the lag shrinks, so this value bounds the nugget from above, up to its sampling error: a fitted nugget well above it is contradicted by the closest pairs.

  • zero_lag_semivariance exists where locations were visited more than once (zero_lag_pairs is not 0). It is the semivariance of every pair of rows that share a location, the variance between visits to one place. That is the measurement part of the nugget, observed and not extrapolated, without the variation at scales below the spacing of the locations, so it bounds the nugget from below. Such pairs are at no lag and in no bin of the variogram, since the model, and so the nugget, describe positive separations.

  • nugget_floor is the value the fit did not let the nugget under: zero_lag_semivariance where it rests on 30 degrees of freedom or more (rows less locations), and 0 otherwise. With detrend = "reml" the model is built from the REML parameters and takes no floor: its nugget can come out below the variance between visits, and nugget_floor is 0.

See also

estimate_sac_range(), which produces the object.

Other spatial autocorrelation: estimate_sac_range(), plot.sac_range()

Examples

library(sf)
# A field with a nugget: half a unit of white noise on a unit sill.
set.seed(3)
n <- 250
xy <- data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000))
D  <- as.matrix(dist(xy))
xy$z <- as.numeric(t(chol(exp(-D / 150) + diag(0.5, n))) %*% rnorm(n))
r <- estimate_sac_range(st_as_sf(xy, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632), "z")
sac_nugget(r)                      # the fitted nugget, on the sill's scale
#> [1] 0.4253438
attr(r, "nugget_at_bound")         # FALSE: an estimate, not the bound
#> [1] FALSE
attr(r, "short_lag_semivariance")  # what the closest pairs say, no model
#> [1] 0.7541593
attr(r, "zero_lag_pairs")          # 0: no location was visited twice
#> [1] 0
sac_nugget(NA)                     # nothing fitted: NA
#> [1] NA
